summary: Iteration 16 — Home dashboard, tab bar, Dress Me flow, Outfits hub, Outfit Detail and Manual Outfit Builder. Backend: 7/7 pytest passed (GET /items, GET /outfits with resolved items, POST /dressme with resolved_items+photo+category, POST/DELETE /outfits, POST /plans set-as-today, duplicate flow). Frontend: Home, Outfits hub, Outfit Detail (Set as Today's Outfit + Duplicate → new /outfit/<id>), Manual Builder (3 slots, per-category pickers, Save+Name modal), and Dress Me itself (loading spinner, 'Perfect for Today', 5-item flat-lay, Save→'Saved to My Outfits', swap sheet) all work with the correct testIDs. Tab bar renders the 5 expected tabs in the correct order (Home · Wardrobe · Dress Me · Outfits · Profile) with sage active tint; Shop/Stylist are correctly hidden (href:null). ONE P0 BLOCKING BUG: opening Dress Me from inside the tab navigator — either via the Home hero `home-dress-me-button` or via the 'Dress Me' tab bar item — crashes the app with 'Maximum update depth exceeded' (React infinite render loop, stack at (tabs)/_layout.tsx:7 → useSyncStore listeners.forEach). Direct URL navigation to /dressme works, so the Dress Me screen itself is fine; the loop is caused by the ambiguous route registration between app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx (which just Redirects to /dressme) and the top-level app/dressme.tsx, combined with the tabPress listener that also calls router.push('/dressme'). Because BOTH primary entrypoints (hero button and tab tap) are broken, the demo path cannot be completed by a user without a browser URL bar — this is the single biggest issue in the iteration and must be fixed before shipping.

ui_bugs.issue: P0 — 'Maximum update depth exceeded' infinite loop when opening Dress Me from inside the tab navigator. Repro (both paths): (1) Home → tap green hero 'Dress Me' button (data-testid=home-dress-me-button) → red-screen React error; (2) tap 'Dress Me' tab bar item → same red-screen. Console stack points at (tabs)/_layout.tsx:7:27 (`const router = useRouter();`) and @react-navigation/core useSyncStore listeners.forEach → forceStoreRerender. Root cause: `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx` renders `<Redirect href='/dressme' />` while `<Tabs.Screen name='dressme'>` in (tabs)/_layout.tsx also has `listeners={{tabPress: (e)=>{e.preventDefault(); router.push('/dressme')}}}`. When the user is inside the (tabs) group and either the listener or the hero calls `router.push('/dressme')`, expo-router prefers the nested `(tabs)/dressme` route, which mounts and immediately Redirects to '/dressme', which resolves back to '(tabs)/dressme', ad infinitum. Direct `page.goto('/dressme')` at a fresh session works because the (tabs) group has not yet been mounted, so the top-level route wins. FIX (one of): (a) delete `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx` and either drop the Dress Me Tabs.Screen entry entirely or replace it with a custom `tabBarButton` that only calls `router.push('/dressme')` (no Tabs.Screen with the same name); OR (b) merge the two files — move the contents of `app/dressme.tsx` into `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx`, drop the tabPress listener, and change the Home hero to `router.push('/(tabs)/dressme')`. Either eliminates the redirect ping-pong.

action_items: FIX (P0 / blocker): resolve the (tabs)/dressme.tsx ↔ app/dressme.tsx redirect ping-pong that causes 'Maximum update depth exceeded' when tapping the Home hero (`home-dress-me-button`) or the 'Dress Me' tab bar entry. Recommended: delete `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx`, drop the `listeners={{tabPress}}` intercept in `_layout.tsx`, and give the Dress Me Tabs.Screen a custom `tabBarButton` that calls `router.push('/dressme')` (without registering an actual screen for that path inside (tabs)). Alternatively, move the whole dressme screen inside the (tabs) group and delete the top-level `app/dressme.tsx`.

After fix, re-run playwright: (1) tap home-dress-me-button from Home → should show 'Building today's outfit' spinner and then 'Perfect for Today' with dressme-item-0..N; (2) tap Dress Me tab from Home → same result; (3) verify the tab bar returns to /(tabs)/index after `router.back()` from Dress Me.

critical_code_review_comments: app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx L1-7: `useRouter()` is called at TabsLayout scope and the `listeners` object `{tabPress: ...}` is re-created every render — this is a well-known expo-router foot-gun. Prefer `useNavigation()` inside the listener or, better, use `tabBarButton` for the Dress Me entry so no listener is needed at all.

app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx: <Redirect> inside a Tabs.Screen guarantees a re-navigation on every focus. Combined with the tabPress listener above, this produces the infinite loop. Redirect is a valid pattern but only when the source and target route are unambiguously different — here the target `/dressme` resolves back to `(tabs)/dressme` because expo-router prefers nested groups.

app/dressme.tsx L38-72: `started` ref + `useEffect(status !== 'idle' && !== 'loading')` correctly auto-runs generate() once and only once; retested and verified working when reached via a fresh /dressme URL.

app/outfit-builder.tsx L75-87: doSave() calls `router.replace(/outfit/${outfit.id})` which is correct (prevents user from back-navigating into the builder mid-save). Verified end-to-end (2 slots picked → Save → name modal → created outfit_fdabdd9960c5 → navigated to detail).

app/outfit/[id].tsx L25-34: `load()` fetches the ENTIRE /outfits list then .find(id) — works for the seeded account but O(N). If a user grows to hundreds of outfits this is wasteful. Consider adding a GET /api/outfits/{id} endpoint (currently missing — only POST/GET-list/DELETE exist).
Backend: /outfits, /dressme, /plans all correctly exclude Mongo `_id` (verified with assert '_id' not in data) and correctly resolve items with photo+category into `items` for the frontend collages.

rca_of_issue: Dress Me tab & hero button infinite render loop — RCA: Two files register the same route name. `app/dressme.tsx` (top-level) is the real Dress Me screen; `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx` is a stub that renders `<Redirect href='/dressme' />` because the design wanted the tab to look like a tab but open a modal-ish full-screen route. In `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` the Dress Me Tabs.Screen has `listeners={{tabPress: (e)=>{e.preventDefault(); router.push('/dressme')}}}`. When the app is running inside the (tabs) navigator and any code path calls `router.push('/dressme')` (either the tabPress listener or Home's `openDressMe → router.push('/dressme')`), expo-router matches the more-specific nested route `(tabs)/dressme` — that mounts, Redirect fires, re-navigates to '/dressme', which again matches (tabs)/dressme, and the `<Tabs>` navigation state store (@react-navigation/core useSyncStore) keeps firing state-change subscribers on every micro-step, exhausting React's setState-in-render budget. `page.goto('/dressme')` on a fresh session works because expo-router initialises without the (tabs) group already mounted, so the initial resolution picks the top-level route unambiguously. Mitigation: (recommended) delete `app/(tabs)/dressme.tsx`; in `_layout.tsx` change the Dress Me entry to `<Tabs.Screen name='dressme-fake' options={{href: null, tabBarButton: (props) => <Pressable {...props} onPress={() => router.push('/dressme')}>...</Pressable>}} />`, OR change `<Tabs.Screen name='dressme' options={{href: null}} />` and render the Dress Me tab icon as an extra Pressable in a custom tab bar. Alternative: move the whole Dress Me screen into `(tabs)/dressme.tsx` (no more top-level file, no Redirect) and drop the tabPress listener + change home hero to `router.push('/(tabs)/dressme')`.
